measure_line: Share of citizens 18 and over who reported voting, November 2024, the ten states with the most voting-age citizens
reading_guide: Each line spans a state’s margin of error at 90 percent confidence, and a gap counts only past the gap’s own margin. A filled dot differs from the nation by more than the margin; an open dot sits within it.
notes_internal: Rule 14.9's correct plate: the script's drawing inside the kit's own figure (ED-E9) until round 2's interval form.
reader_question: Which of the largest states differ from the nation in reported turnout, past the margin of error?
title: Five of the ten states with the most voting-age citizens differed from the nation’s 65.3 percent turnout by more than the margin of error.
notes: Past the margin: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Florida, New York and Texas. Within it: Ohio, Illinois, California, North Carolina and Georgia.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey Voting and Registration Supplement, Table 4a, reported voting for states, November 2024, 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Self-reported voting among citizens 18 and over; state margins of error reach 5.6 points.
alt: Dots with margin of error lines for ten states’ reported turnout in 2024 against the nation’s 65.3 percent: five past the margin, five within it.
